title: Vision Transformers and Multimodal Meaning · Level 3
slo: Explain how image and text information can be connected in a multimodal model.

exercises.question_text: What kind of training data helps combine language and vision encoders?

options.rationale: Each image is linked to associated language in this training data. These pairs support combining language and vision encoders.
One class label identifies an image category. It does not provide the descriptive language needed for image-text pairing.
options.better_fit: Images with class labels are appropriate for training image classifiers.

feedback.intrinsic: This supports naming a subject but not linking images to language.
feedback.instructional: Multimodal training uses images paired with text descriptions.

options.rationale: Bounding boxes identify object locations. They do not pair an image with a written description.
options.better_fit: Images with bounding boxes are appropriate for training object detectors.

feedback.intrinsic: This identifies where objects are, not how images connect to words.
feedback.instructional: Paired descriptions provide the language connection.

options.rationale: Pixel classes mark regions within an image. They do not supply associated textual descriptions.
options.better_fit: Images with pixel classes are appropriate for training semantic-segmentation models.

feedback.intrinsic: This defines object areas but no descriptive language.

exercises.explanation: Paired images and descriptions enable language and vision encoders to be combined.

exercises.question_text: How can a combined language-and-vision model describe a new image? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The model first identifies visual features in the new image. Those features supply the visual information for interpretation.
Recognized visual features can be related to language. Associated language supplies words for the description.
The shared vector space contains related visual and language representations. Searching it supports finding language associated with the image features.
A single label supplies only a category name. It does not provide the richer semantic interpretation of a description.
options.better_fit: One class label is appropriate for a simple image-classification task.

feedback.intrinsic: The image would receive a category rather than a written description.
feedback.instructional: Description links visual features with associated language in shared space.

exercises.explanation: Description uses visual features, associated language, and shared space.

exercises.question_text: A language vocabulary represents relationships among words, whereas a visual vocabulary represents relationships among visual features.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would blur the distinction between word and image-feature representations.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Language vocabulary encodes word relationships; visual vocabulary encodes visual-feature relationships.

exercises.explanation: The two vocabularies represent different modalities.

exercises.question_text: When hat-like and head-like features occur together, a vision transformer understands hats and heads as humans do.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This claims more than the learned visual pattern supports.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The model relates visual characteristics but does not understand objects as people do.

exercises.explanation: It can infer a visual relationship without human-like understanding.

exercises.question_text: Which features can visual embeddings encode? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Color is a visual feature in an image. Visual embeddings can encode it alongside other features.
Shape is a visual property of image content. Visual embeddings can represent shape-related patterns.
Texture describes a visual surface pattern. Visual embeddings can encode texture with other image features.
Word meaning is represented by language embeddings. It is not itself a visual feature encoded by visual embeddings.
options.better_fit: Word meaning is appropriate when working with a language vocabulary.

feedback.intrinsic: This would shift from image features to text.
feedback.instructional: Visual embeddings encode image features such as color, shape, contrast, and texture.

exercises.explanation: Visual embeddings can encode multiple visual features.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: That choice does not name the common representation.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use shared vector space for the unified multimodal representation.

exercises.explanation: A shared vector space is the unified representation for related language and visual embeddings.

exercises.question_text: A team receives a previously unseen customer photo and needs the model to produce a written scene description. Which capability should it use?

options.rationale: Image description connects visual features with associated language. It gives semantic interpretation beyond a single category.
Classification predicts a main-subject category. That is the narrower capability named in the question.
options.better_fit: Image classification is appropriate when the goal is to identify a fruit type.

feedback.intrinsic: The result would be only a category name.
feedback.instructional: Image description provides semantic interpretation beyond one label.

options.rationale: Detection identifies locations of objects in an image. It does not itself generate a language description.
options.better_fit: Detecting object regions is appropriate when locating several items in a scene.

feedback.intrinsic: The result could show locations but not describe the scene.
feedback.instructional: Description requires language associated with visual features.

options.rationale: Pixel classification assigns a class to each image area. It does not produce a written interpretation of the scene.
options.better_fit: Classifying image pixels is appropriate for semantic segmentation.

feedback.intrinsic: The result could outline objects without explaining them in words.
feedback.instructional: Semantic interpretation creates an image description.

exercises.explanation: Describing an unfamiliar image goes beyond one label.

exercises.question_text: Order the pieces to form a correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The contrast between the two vocabularies becomes unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: State the visual vocabulary's role first, then explain that the language vocabulary maps relationships among words.

exercises.correct_answer: A visual vocabulary maps relationships among visual features, while a language vocabulary maps relationships among words
exercises.explanation: A visual vocabulary maps semantic relationships among visual features, while a language vocabulary maps semantic relationships among words.

exercises.question_text: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The sentence obscures which embeddings are connected.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Name the technique, then state the relationship, the two embedding types, and the shared space.

exercises.correct_answer: Cross-model attention relates language embeddings with vision embeddings in shared space
exercises.explanation: Cross-model attention relates language embeddings with vision embeddings in shared space.

exercises.question_text: What can paired images and text descriptions enable? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Paired data aligns image information with descriptive language. This supports combining language and vision encoders.
Descriptions link language representations to image representations. This can connect language and visual vocabularies.
Combined language and vision encoders form a multimodal model. Paired image-text data helps train that combination.
Paired training links language and visual embeddings. It does not eliminate the visual representations needed for images.
options.better_fit: Visual embeddings remain appropriate for representing features extracted from images.

feedback.intrinsic: Removing visual embeddings would remove the image-side representation.
feedback.instructional: Paired training combines and links both embedding types.

exercises.explanation: Paired data links language and vision rather than replacing either.

rather than understanding objects as humans do.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: That choice shifts from image patterns to language.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: This concept concerns visual characteristics that co-occur in images.

exercises.explanation: The model infers relationships among visual characteristics or features.

exercises.question_text: What do vision transformers create to represent visual features and their relationships?

options.rationale: Visual embeddings are vectors representing image features. They also capture contextual relationships among those features.
Language tokens are units used to process text. They do not represent visual relationships in an image.
options.better_fit: Language tokens are appropriate when a model processes written words.

feedback.intrinsic: This would process text rather than image content.
feedback.instructional: Visual embeddings represent features in image patches.

options.rationale: An image label names a predicted category. It does not encode rich relationships among visual features.
options.better_fit: Image labels are appropriate for basic image-classification outputs.

feedback.intrinsic: This would return a category instead of a feature representation.

options.rationale: Bounding boxes locate regions containing objects. They do not encode contextual visual features.
options.better_fit: Bounding boxes are appropriate when locating objects in an image.

feedback.intrinsic: This would mark locations without representing image features.
feedback.instructional: Visual embeddings represent features and their relationships.

exercises.explanation: Visual embeddings represent visual features and their relationships.
